qa.name: Flexor Hallucis Brevis
qa.origin: Plantar surface of the cuboid and lateral cuneiforms; plantar calcaneocuboid ligament
qa.insertion: Two heads: medial head to medial sesamoid and medial base of proximal phalanx of great toe; lateral head to lateral sesamoid and lateral base of proximal phalanx
qa.function: Flexes the MTP joint of the great toe; the two sesamoid bones within its tendons protect the FHL tendon and bear weight during push-off
qa.opposing_muscle: Extensor Hallucis Longus and Brevis (great toe extension)
qa.clinical_note: Flexor Hallucis Brevis contains two sesamoid bones (medial and lateral) within its tendons at the MTP joint of the great toe — these are the only sesamoids consistently present in the foot and bear significant weight during the push-off phase of gait. Sesamoiditis (inflammation of these bones) causes pain under the first MTP joint in runners and dancers. Bipartite sesamoids (divided into two parts) can be mistaken for fractures on X-ray. FHB is innervated by the medial plantar nerve (L5–S1).

qa.name: Adductor Hallucis
qa.origin: Oblique head: bases of metatarsals 2–4 and sheath of fibularis longus tendon. Transverse head: plantar MTP ligaments of toes 3–5
qa.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe; lateral sesamoid bone
qa.innervation: Lateral plantar nerve, deep branch (S1, S2)
qa.function: Adducts the great toe toward the second toe; assists in flexion of the MTP joint; supports the transverse arch of the foot
qa.blood_supply: Lateral plantar artery; plantar metatarsal arteries
qa.clinical_note: Adductor Hallucis has two heads — oblique and transverse — analogous to Adductor Pollicis in the hand. The transverse head is the key maintainer of the transverse arch. In hallux valgus, the lateral pull of Adductor Hallucis combined with the medial deviation of the first metatarsal progressively worsens the deformity. Surgical correction (osteotomy) may include lateral soft tissue release of the adductor tendon. It is innervated by the deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve — same nerve as the interossei.

qa.name: Flexor Digiti Minimi Brevis
qa.origin: Base of the fifth metatarsal and sheath of fibularis longus tendon
qa.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the little toe
qa.innervation: Lateral plantar nerve, superficial branch (S1, S2)
qa.function: Flexes the MTP joint of the little toe
qa.clinical_note: Flexor Digiti Minimi Brevis is the plantar equivalent of the hand's Flexor Digiti Minimi Brevis. It originates from the fifth metatarsal base — adjacent to where Fibularis Brevis inserts and where avulsion fractures (dancer's fracture) commonly occur. It is innervated by the superficial branch of the lateral plantar nerve, distinguishing it from Adductor Hallucis (deep branch). Note: also covered in Hand — Hypothenar as its anatomical counterpart.
